final_synthesis: The ozone hole was primarily caused by manufactured halocarbon refrigerants, solvents, propellants, and foam-blowing agents such as chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) and hydrochlorofluorocarbons (HCFCs), which are referred to as ozone-depleting substances (ODS). These compounds were transported into the stratosphere where ultraviolet light broke them apart, releasing chlorine atoms that catalytically destroy thousands of ozone molecules [S1][S2]. Nearly 99% of banned ozone-depleting substances have been phased out under the Montreal Protocol. If current policies continue, the ozone layer is expected to recover to 1980 values by about 2040 globally, around 2045 over the Arctic and around 2066 over the Antarctic [S3]. Despite this progress, unexpected emissions of CFC-11 from eastern China in the 2010s temporarily slowed ozone layer recovery but have since decreased with enforcement measures [S4].
